Subject: AtlasHealth: SCCs/UK Addendum sequencing + TIA gating

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Legal is after two things before we can route a commercial contract to procurement: (1) a clear sequencing plan that shows which SCCs will be in place vs. when the UK Addendum (IDTA) is delivered; and (2) a TIA/DTIA gating plan so our Privacy team can sign off on production data flows.

We pulled together a short list of must-haves and some target timelines — attaching the high-level questions (atlas_tia_questions.pdf) for your intake. Can Redwood produce a remediations sequence and a Mutual Action Plan that maps SCC vs UK Addendum deliverables, plus a checklist of evidence we can expect at each gate?

High level asks:
- Which SCCs are already implemented versus those needing contract addenda?
- How will Redwood indicate model/data residency and KV cache routing for EU-origin traffic?
- Proposed gating criteria for turning on production traffic (TIA pass criteria).
- Expected lead times for any subprocessor attestations we will need.

Could we have a draft MTP and sequencing by Tuesday EOD (11/3)? If it helps, loop in legal and product.

Best,
Carlos
VP, Legal Ops
AtlasHealth
(attachment: atlas_tia_questions.pdf)

Subject: Re: AtlasHealth: SCCs/UK Addendum sequencing + TIA gating

Carlos — thanks for the clear asks and the doc. We'll own the sequencing deliverable and the Mutual Action Plan. High level reply below and we'll follow up with a packet by Tue EOD.

Quick answers (top of inbox):
- Redwood has the EU Commission SCCs implemented in our hosted API contract; the UK Addendum is a separate addendum we can execute and we can provide a timeline for rolling it out in the contract repo.
- For EU-origin traffic we can pin region / onshore fallback via the routing policy. KV cache residency is documented and we will include explicit evidence on cache segmentation in the packet.
- Proposed TIA pass criteria: completed TIA questionnaire + evidence bundle (subprocessor attestations for any processors with cross-border transit, encryption-at-rest configuration, logging/trace proof-of-delivery), and one successful staging run with production-like sample.
- Subprocessor attestations: typical lead time is 7–14 business days depending on vendor responsiveness; we will flag any vendor that needs a longer timeline.

Plan: Jonas will draft the SCC/UKAddendum breakpoint map, Kim will scope the evidence checklist and LAURA will draft a Mutual Action Plan doc. I'll assemble and send the packet (redwood_scc_mapping.pdf, tia-gap-log.csv, mtp-atlashealth-v1.docx) and include a suggested canary gating cadence.

Are you available for a 30-min sync Monday (11/2) 10–11am PT to align on acceptance criteria?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Privacy & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Rishi / Kim — attaching the draft SCC vs UK Addendum breakpoint map for AtlasHealth (see inline). High level notes:

- We treat SCCs as the baseline (contract executed in current hosted terms). The UK Addendum is scoped as an add-on that requires signature but no infra change for most customers; where residency is required we enable routing flags and provide evidence.
- For AtlasHealth I recommend a two-phase rollout: Phase 1 = contract addendum + onshore routing for EU production traffic limited to 10% of sessions (canary) and Phase 2 = full routing + attestation completion.
- Canary gating criteria: 0 P0 security findings during 72h, no elevated latency >50ms P50 delta, evidence of KV cache segmentation.

I'll fold these into redwood_scc_mapping.pdf and add a short table of subprocessor lead-times.

Jonas
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
